title: GPU matrix multiplication (half precision)
short_description: Large half precision matrix multiplication through the vendor's own maths library.

structured_text.description: Multiplies a pair of large half precision matrices on the graphics processor, using the maths library the hardware vendor ships for exactly this job. The matrices are sized to fill a meaningful share of graphics memory, so the result depends on the whole stack: the matrix units, the memory hierarchy that feeds them, and the quality of the vendor's own software.
structured_text.metric_explanation: Throughput is the number of half precision operations per second during the multiply, in billions, reported in GFLOPS.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. This is the figure that most directly predicts training and inference speed, since both are dominated by matrix multiplication at this scale.
structured_text.reasoning: The raw compute tests measure how fast the matrix units can be driven in isolation. Real machine learning work reaches those units through a vendor library, on matrices far too large to keep on chip, and how much of the peak survives that journey is what actually decides performance.
